assumptions: Both legs work symmetrically, so laterality is bilateral.
The set is counted in repetitions.
The concentric phase is hip extension from the floor, with the knees held at a roughly fixed flexed angle.
Hands rest on or steady the bar, but grip is not a primary demand because the bar is supported on the hips.
The upper back and feet stay on the floor, which makes this a closed-chain movement.
The spine stays neutral, so the lumbar spine is not a primary mover.
classification_reasons: Supine barbell glute bridge with the bar across the hips; the instructions and both frames agree on a bilateral hip-extension movement driven through the heels.
The movement is a bilateral hip extension with the feet and upper back as fixed supports, so it fits the closed-chain hip_hinge family and the available vocabulary.
